title.narrative: CAFOD and CA Pilot Lebanon: Microgrants in emergency

description.narrative:
CAFOD and CA have been engaged in innovative piloting across the Middle East together since the start of the TSEQ response in Feb 2023. In Lebanon, during the design workshop for the locally led pooled fund project one of the key gaps identified during this engagement is the need to pilot a mechanism for CA and CAFOD to provide micro-grants to community groups during a crisis without having to go through a full partnership onboarding process. This is in line with the CA Humanitarian signature, our external commitments on risk sharing and quality funding (Grand Bargain), and our working with diverse partners commitment as a convenor, catalyser, and connecter as articulated in the Target Operating Model
The pilot is led by CAFOD with CA providing technical input, and co-funding. The project was proposed in November 2025 based on the security analysis that there would be a sudden, and significant escalation of the crisis in Lebanon in early 2026. This escalation has taken place on the 28th Feb 2026.
During the last crisis in Lebanon a large number of informal community groups came together to support displaced people. One example of this was an activist in Tripoli who engaged 400 volunteers to provide hot meals in shelters. The activist placed more than $2,500 on his credit card in order to meet volunteer travel costs. A micro-grant (up to £3,000) would provide an outsized impact on these groups and would allow us to work with a diverse group of initiatives alongside our pre-existing partners.
